title: Invoke compatibility proto mapper and decision telemetry
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Adds an OpenAI-compatibility proto mapper that normalizes function/tool invocation envelopes to Redwood internal shapes. Introduces an explicit decision telemetry event (invoke.decision) that records tool selection candidates, normalized scores, and final chosen tool to aid post-deployment debugging. Default rollout: gradual on Hosted, opt-in for Dedicated/Private until config flag 'openai_compat_proto_mapper' enabled.

description: Motivation: Customers expect OpenAI-style function/tool calling to 'just work' when routed through Redwood's serving runtime. However, in practice we see a set of recurring issues: heterogeneous tool descriptors from third-party models, ambiguous tool_choice semantics when multiple tools match, and stream fragmentation that splits the tool invocation payload across SSE boundaries. This PR introduces a compatibility-focused proto mapper and decision telemetry that together make tool invocation more deterministic and observable.Design summary: 1) proto_mapper: a lightweight rule engine that canonicalizes incoming OpenAI-compatible invocation envelopes into a single Redwood internal representation. It normalizes fields (name/description/schema/arguments), expands legacy aliases into canonical redwood_tool_id, and attaches a compat_hint when the mapping required heuristics. Mappings are deterministic and extensible via a small YAML ruleset shipped with the package. 2) choice_scorer: when multiple tools match a requested function name/schema, the scorer computes an ordered candidate list using schema affinity (how well the provided arguments conform to each tool schema), stream-priming context (tokens already generated that imply certain tool semantics), and operational priors (recent latency/cost observed for the customer's tenant). The winner receives an explicit confidence score and a short rationale encoded in metadata. 3) stream_coordinator: improves streaming stability by aligning fragments to logical tool frames: partial JSON fragments are buffered and resynchronized rather than forwarded to downstream tool adapters; we emit a fragment_resync event for observability. 4) telemetry: emit an invoke.decision event for every tool invocation that contains candidate list, scores, chosen_index, confidence, request_id, and quick pointers to the proto_mapper rule that fired. This event is low-cardinality and intended for debugging regressions and production investigations.Changes and files: See changed_files for a compact list. Key behavioral changes are limited and guarded behind a feature flag 'openai_compat_proto_mapper' that defaults to on for Hosted only and off for Dedicated/Private until customers opt in. Tests: added unit tests covering nested JSON arguments, missing schema resolution, alias expansion, and integration tests that simulate streaming SSE fragmentation across multiple boundaries to verify deterministic reassembly and correct candidate scoring. Performance: choice_scorer is designed to be cheap (fast schema affinity checks and cached token-based signals). Benchmarks on a 4k sequence workload show median decision latency ~= 0.9ms additional per-invoke at p50 and 2.4ms at p95 under load (detailed numbers in benchmark artifact attached to CI). Rollout and risk mitigation: rollout is staged. Hosted -> 10%/50%/100% over two weeks with monitoring dashboards. Dedicated/Private customers will see release notes and can enable via console or config. We included a migration script to generate alias mappings for large customers that rely on legacy tool names.Open questions and future work: - Consider surfacing the decision rationale in debug traces for customers with private deployments. - Expand rule engine to accept safe machine-suggested mappings (requires guardrails). - Add optional delta compression for repeated identical invocation envelopes to reduce egress cost.Review conversation snapshot: See review_thread field for representative comments. Merge strategy: squash; small logical commits squashed to a single logical change and merged to main.Approvals: Approved by core runtime reviewers and SRE, CI passed and manual integration harness validated in staging.
review_thread: Ethan Park: Nice separation of concerns. Two asks before merge: tightened unit tests for alias collisions and a short doc paragraph on security implications of compat_hint.
Maya Chen (author): Added tests for alias collision and documented compat_hint semantics in docs/openai_compatibility.md. compat_hint is a low-entropy string and does not include sensitive args.

Liam O'Connor: Optional nit: can we avoid constructing full JSON blobs when a fragment is small? Suggest a fast-path in stream_coordinator. Response: added fast-path to return on single-fragment invocations without buffering.
Priya Desai: Telemetry schema looks good. Confirmed low-cardinality fields only. Approved +1.

QA Lead (Ravi Patel): Ran integration harness against staging with 50k synthetic invokes. Observed 0.02% additional failures attributable to edge-case mapping; mitigated by fallback to legacy mapper. Added a hotfix backout flag.
